official_secure_channel_note: Use only the named official website, secure HTTPS form, verified office phone, or in-person office path for sensitive case details and documents. If the current public instructions do not show a secure submission path, call the responsible election office first before sending records.
minimum_necessary_disclosure_note: Send only the personal information the current official process requires. Do not post or send full Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, dates of birth, confidential residence details, court papers, custody records, or other sensitive identifiers through public, unverified, or generalized channels.
operability_now_note: Before relying on this path under same-day or near-cutoff pressure, verify that the responsible office, portal, site, or delivery route is still open and operating right now using the latest official hours/closure notice, current update page, or verified office phone.
deadline_imminence_note: Do not assume an older FAQ, PDF, screenshot, or cached directory still controls today's path. If the cutoff is near or may already have passed, confirm the current live deadline with the responsible office and pivot immediately to the stated fallback or confirmation path if the original route is no longer operable.
current_official_controls_note: The current directly governing state or local election-office source controls for this case. National routing pages, generalized official explainers, and archive summaries are routing aids only and are not substitutes for the current official instruction that directly governs the voter's jurisdiction and election scope.
superseding_notice_note: Older pages, PDFs, screenshots, packet inserts, or archived summaries may remain visible. Follow the most current official notice, form, correction, update, or replacement instruction and use the dated or last-updated cue when available.
unresolved_conflict_stop_note: If current official materials still materially conflict, disagree, or leave a controlling gap, do not synthesize an answer from fragments. Treat that unresolved conflict as a stop condition and use the responsible official office or help path for case-specific confirmation; move to the rights/safety escalation lane when the conflict is paired with likely wrongful denial, intimidation, discrimination, or unsafe exposure.

problem_classes.plain_language: If your ballot was lost after issuance, request a replacement through the official help path and do not return the original ballot if it later appears unless instructed to do so.
problem_classes.time_sensitive_note: Request replacement before the stated office cutoff or use the in-person fallback.

problem_classes.plain_language: If you made a mistake or damaged the ballot, return the spoiled ballot if required and follow the replacement instructions rather than crossing out marks.
problem_classes.time_sensitive_note: Bring or mail the spoiled ballot to the elections office before using the reissued ballot.

problem_classes.plain_language: If only the return envelope is unusable, download the replacement-envelope packet or contact the elections office for one.
problem_classes.time_sensitive_note: The replacement-envelope packet does not include a ballot.

reissue_paths.plain_language: Use the online replacement request form until the online cutoff; after that point, use an in-person path.
Visit the elections office to replace a lost or spoiled ballot or to return a damaged ballot and receive a reissued ballot.
Use this path only when the ballot remains usable and the voter needs a replacement envelope packet.
If replacement delivery is no longer practical and the original mail ballot has not been returned, the voter may vote a regular ballot during early voting after completing the required affirmation.
If the voter cannot surrender the original mail ballot on Election Day, the voter must use the provisional fallback path.

affirmation_or_form_notes: A voter who reports a lost, spoiled, or never-received ballot must complete the stated affirmation before a reissued ballot is counted.
A replacement-envelope packet does not itself void the previously issued ballot.

surrender_policy.plain_language: Return or surrender the original ballot when the public instructions require it. If you cannot surrender it, follow the explicit fallback-ballot instructions rather than assuming the original ballot is automatically void.

in_person_fallbacks.plain_language: The voter may vote a regular ballot during early voting after affirming the original mail ballot is lost or unusable.
The voter must vote provisionally on Election Day if the original mail ballot cannot be surrendered and has not already been returned.

freshness_note: Re-verify office cutoffs, satellite office availability, downloadable packet links, and in-person fallback instructions during the final week before the election.
